implementation.arena_only: Acquire uses spare only when mode is ARENA and spare is nonempty; release extracts only when mode is ARENA and spare is empty. SYSTEM retains ordinary emplace/erase semantics. SYSTEM still has an added mode check and the opaque domain field, so no unchanged-performance assertion is justified.
implementation.fresh_ids: take_id is still mutex-protected, strictly increasing, non-recycling and stops before overflow. A reused node receives both fresh key and complete Lease mapped value before insertion; stale public IDs cannot find the detached node.
implementation.publication_order: All access, owner/pending, range and reader/writer checks precede take_id. Map insert/emplace precedes reader/writer updates and out publication. A local node handle owns the extracted node if insertion throws; the existing guarded boundary handles failure without publishing a lease.
implementation.allocator: The node is extracted from and reinserted into the same domain LeaseMap. Its retained allocator therefore matches the target allocator. Production uses std::allocator; no map type or allocator swap occurs. Successful insertion transfers ownership and leaves the temporary insert_return_type node empty.
implementation.release_order: Lease attributes are read before extraction. After extract/erase, no lease iterator or node reference is used. The allocation reference belongs to the independent allocation map, and last-lease retirement preserves existing owner/backing cleanup.
implementation.idle_node: spare_lease is not counted as a live lease and contains only an inert old allocation ID and writer bool. Its mapped value is overwritten on reuse; it owns no Backing or external/provider context.
implementation.maintenance: reclaim_all clears the independent spare after the poison guard and before backing detach/unlock/callbacks. Both callers require quiet under the same mutex. Arena reset retains spare; normal trim/collect releases it. Destroy provides RAII fallback.
implementation.sentinel: Clearing the extracted node handle deallocates only that independent node through its original allocator. The leases map sentinel and active container storage are not released or reconstructed.
implementation.quarantine: The existing provider_poisoned early return may retain at most one idle cached lease node along with the quarantined domain. Unknown claims/charges and no-retry callback rules are unchanged. This is not leak-freedom evidence.
implementation.abi: The public mgmem_domain remains opaque and no public header or capability contract changes. Internal domain size and metadata retention still require separate measurement/disclosure.

callback_unlock_analysis: On an Arena external last-lease release, the map node can enter spare, the allocation record is retired, and reclaim_standalone detaches the Backing before unlocking. pending increments before unlock and prevents quiet collect/destroy.

While the external callback is executing, another thread may borrow an existing other owner and consume/release the spare. The outer release frame never dereferences its old lease iterator or cached node after extraction; reclaim_standalone uses only its detached Backing and post-callback ledger fields.

The cached Lease stores no Backing pointer, so reusing its storage cannot invalidate the detached external Backing. Each other borrow/release operation accesses the shared spare under the domain mutex.

Full reclaim_all begins quiet and sets maintenance before unlocking. There is no live allocation available for a successful borrow, and new allocation is blocked by maintenance; a cleared spare cannot become an active lease through that full-reclaim callback window.

Existing provider/external callbacks remain outside domain and registry locks. Same-domain callback reentry remains forbidden by the original contract; the review covers separate-thread API work on an existing other owner, not unsupported direct callback reentry.

controller.AB_BA: Even pair count 2..16 is required; each profile alternates baseline/candidate and candidate/baseline, so AB and BA counts are balanced. Shapes/batches/modes/executors remain separate profile summaries.
controller.identity: Each process gets the same staged executable hash and one selected runtime copy verified against captured hashes. Native validation confirms reported module path plus disk bytes; this is path/disk identity, not mapped-page attestation.
controller.matched_work: Native validator checks independent byte oracle, payload and operation counts, logical metadata operations, peak live lease records, preparation counts/bytes, raw timing consistency and CLOSED_ZERO. Pair comparison requires matching semantic fields; physical allocator counts are intentionally allowed to differ.
controller.raw_metrics: validate recomputes nearest-rank P50/P95 and throughput from every raw cycle/round, requires finite reported values and exact metric names, and checks nonnegative raw durations with positive hot time.
controller.zero_baseline: If a validated baseline metric is zero, pair ratio is None and the absolute delta is still kept. A group with all zero baselines yields median None rather than fake ratio 1, infinity or an empty-median error. Defined ratios alone enter the ratio median, while every original None remains in the pair records.
controller.failures: Nonzero child status, nonblank stderr, malformed JSON, identity/semantic/metric mismatch or timeout keeps an incomplete receipt and returns nonzero. Timeout partial streams are retained; no retries or exclusions exist.
controller.scope: Prepared-stream and held-stage lifetimes have different workload IDs/peak leases and must not be combined. Worker outer timing is not pure library cost, and the controller correctly labels observations as descriptive non-product data.

nonblocking_reporting_notes: When publishing medians for metrics with zero baseline, disclose defined and undefined pair counts; the compact controller summary does not directly include those counts although all pair values are preserved.
The printed processes count is attempted runs, not necessarily completed runs on failure. Only PASS_SCOPED rows may count as completed observations; state and row details prevent accidental success.

Source hashes in the controller are recorded at entry; the outer frozen plan/build receipt remains necessary to bind compiled artifacts and historical source closure continuously. Runtime and executable staging hashes are checked for each process.
No System performance invariance, lower RSS, Android runtime benefit or all-interleavings proof follows from this read-only review.
